The martyrdom of Mamosta Mohammad Nezhati, following a terrorist and brutal crime by American-Zionist separatist groups, has caused sorrow among the religious community and people of West Azarbaijan Province, the IRGC said in a statement on Wednesday.
​
This crime is not merely the targeting of a prominent figure, but also a desperate attempt to create rifts among Muslims, to undermine Shia-Sunni unity, and to disrupt security and peace in society, it added.
​
Since the victory of the Islamic Revolution, West Azarbaijan Province has always faced such incidents; however, the unity between Shia and Sunni Muslims has not been undermined in the slightest, and this has certainly strengthened the bond between the followers of these two sects, it noted.

📄 IRGC urges media to preserve Iran’s social cohesion

📌 Arak, IRNA – The Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) has urged Iranian media outlets to preserve the social solidarity and public cohesion that emerged during the recent conflicts against the country.

Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi, the IRGC’s public relations deputy and spokesperson, said on Wednesday that media organizations should accurately and continuously document national unity and strengthen public confidence in Iran’s domestic capabilities.
​
Mohebbi described the recent conflict as multidimensional, involving military, cognitive, technological, economic and geopolitical aspects. He said artificial intelligence, drones, sensors, software systems and commercial data played major roles in intelligence gathering, targeting and operations.
​
He also highlighted the strategic importance of Iran’s geography, particularly the Strait of Hormuz, saying developments there could affect global energy, transportation and supply chains.
​
The IRGC official said journalists play a key role in the media warfare, where public perceptions, confidence and determination are central. He urged media outlets to counter psychological operations and prevent economic pressures and wartime costs from weakening public morale.
​
Mohebbi praised journalists for reflecting public participation and connecting society with national defense efforts, calling on them to continue documenting achievements and strengthening social cohesion.

🔻 US sanctions will not stop Iran’s aviation industry: Official

📌 Tehran, IRNA — The head of Iran’s Civil Aviation Organization says new US sanctions against Iranian airlines are a continuation of a failed policy, stressing that they may raise costs but cannot halt the country’s flight operations.

Reacting to Washington’s decision to blacklist 27 Iranian airlines, Captain Abouzar Shiroudi said on Wednesday that the move is neither innovative nor effective.
​
He noted that Iran’s aviation industry has faced restrictions for decades but has continued to operate thanks to the resilience and expertise of its specialists.
​
Targeting airlines is effectively a restriction on the public, since aviation is vital infrastructure serving millions of passengers, patients, students and businesses, he added.
​
Despite restrictions on aircraft purchases, parts and services, Iranian airlines remain operational, and flights will continue under full safety standards, Shiroudi emphasized.
